title: Caret stability for tokenized contenteditable inputs: preserve selection and reduce jumpiness
creator: Marisol Gómez
description:
Problem: our tokenized multi-value input (used for recipients, tags, and rule-expressions) relies on contenteditable wrappers for rich behavior. On a set of platforms and edge cases (mobile IME, long paste, browser autofill, and when tokens are recycled during reflow) the caret jumps to the end or selection collapses unexpectedly. This causes frequent user frustration and produces lost input when users are typing quickly or accepting suggested completions.

Goal: define a stable, cross-platform caret-preservation pattern and interaction heuristics for our contenteditable-backed token inputs. Produce design guidance, a small interaction spec for engineering, and an acceptance checklist that prevents regressions. Include fallbacks for browsers where precise caret restores are unreliable and ensure ARIA behavior for screen readers remains correct.
acceptance_criteria: When a token is added/removed or tokens reflow, the visible caret position is preserved for >95% of interactions in e2e tests (mobile + desktop) rather than jumping to end-of-line.
Screen reader announcement behavior does not become more verbose: dynamic error/helper messages remain under existing aria-live guidance.

Edge-case flows covered in tests: paste of comma/space separated list, IME composition commit, undo (Cmd/Ctrl+Z), and programmatic token dedupe. These flows have automated integration tests in the repo.

Design doc and code comments include explicit fallback behavior for older Safari/Android WebView versions and recommendation for a keyboard-only alternative control when caret preservation is impossible.
New visual regressions do not appear in Percy snapshots for token inputs across three density themes and dark/light tokens.
design_notes: Prefer minimal DOM churn: avoid full innerHTML replacements on every keystroke. Use targeted DOM updates around cursor node when possible.
Introduce a micro-protocol for engineering: before mutation -> snapshot caret (node, offset); after mutation -> attempt restore; if restore fails, apply heuristic restore (nearest token boundary).

Define heuristic order: exact restore -> anchor by data-token-id -> restore by character offset inside nearest text node -> fall back to collapsed caret at logical insertion point (not necessarily end-of-line).
Provide explicit guidance for selection ranges vs collapsed caret (we treat range selection as higher-fidelity and attempt to restore both anchors).
Recommend exposing a small events API: onCaretStabilized, onRestoreFailure to allow analytics and targeted debugging in production.
engineering_notes: Work with ENG to implement snapshot/restore util in packages/ui/form-token-inputs and add integration tests in cypress/emulation-mode for mobile keyboards.
Avoid third-party contenteditable libs; create lightweight util that understands our token data attributes (data-token-id, data-token-type).
Quantify performance: snapshot/restore should add <2ms median on desktop and <8ms on low-end mobile during token-heavy updates (<20 tokens).
Add unit tests around IME composition: compositionstart/compositionend events with simulated commits (Japanese/Chinese).
Add feature flag (design.caretStabilityV1) to allow staged rollout and quick rollback if a regression is detected.
tasks: Design: write micro-spec and produce 3 interaction diagrams (desktop typing, mobile IME commit, paste-dedupe flow).
Design: update token input Figma frame with visible caret visual states and annotate accessible label offsets.
Eng: implement snapshot/restore util and wire into token input component (packages/ui).
Eng: add e2e scenarios covering paste, IME, undo, and rapid token insert/remove sequences.
QA: run regression sweep across density themes and run accessibility audit with VoiceOver/TalkBack
Ship: enable behind feature flag, dark launch to internal app, monitor for 72 hours, then roll to 100% if stable.
